Harbor Bridge reopens after 18-month repair

By Staff Reporter

The Harbor Bridge in Port Elm reopened to traffic on Monday after an 18-month repair project.

The repairs cost 240 million dollars, according to the city.

Mayor Dana Whitfield said traffic should return to normal by Friday.

About 45,000 vehicles crossed the bridge each day before it closed.

Engineers replaced the deck and strengthened the towers against earthquakes.

Local shops near the waterfront said business fell by a third during the closure.

The state transportation agency paid for most of the work.
